title: JSON-RPC error.data for subscribe/unsubscribe rejections
description: Shape of the `data` member of a JSON-RPC error returned by Labby's resources/subscribe or resources/unsubscribe. Produced by build_agent_error_value() via crates/labby/src/mcp/agent_error.rs. This is the versioned agent recovery contract owned by docs/contracts/agent-error-contract.md — this schema narrows it to the subscription surface and does not redefine it.

contract_version.description: Agent error contract version. Asserted in crates/labby/src/mcp/agent_error.rs tests.

kind.description: Stable error kind. `not_found` is emitted by the resource_not_found constructor for gates G-3 (route scope) and G-4 (snapshot membership); `budget_exceeded` for gate G-5 (per-session subscription cap). The originally-planned `unsupported_protocol_method` kind was removed after review: rmcp rejects modern sessions before the handler runs (handler/server.rs:185-201), so gate G-2 and its error kind were never real work. Both kinds here are already registered in labby-runtime's classification tables, so no ERRORS.md spec change is required.

message.description: Human-readable message, mirrored from the JSON-RPC error.message.

service.description: The surface that produced the error, not the resource's owning upstream. Follows the precedent set in crates/labby/src/mcp/resource_errors.rs.

action.description: Dispatch action name; matches the `action` field of the corresponding tracing event.

properties.$comment_error_code: Gates G-3 and G-4 use JSON-RPC -32002. This is era-correct and must not be 'fixed' to -32602: SEP-2164 (merged 2026-05-18) moved resource-not-found to -32602 for protocol 2026-07-28 while retaining -32002 as a client-side back-compat accept, and this handler serves only pre-2026-07-28 sessions. Gate G-5 uses -32602 (invalid params). See CONTRACT.md C-17.

resource.description: The URI the caller requested. Echoed back so the agent can correlate without re-parsing its own request.

origin.description: Where the failure arose. Subscription rejections use `discovery` — including out-of-scope denials, which must not surface as `policy` or they would be distinguishable from not-found (contract C-4).

recovery.description: What the agent should do next.

action.description: `rediscover` for an unknown or out-of-scope URI (the default for kind `not_found`, so it needs no explicit override); `retry_later` only when the URI is catalog-listed but absent from the ack snapshot, i.e. the upstream-reconnect window (contract C-5) — this is the one case that does require an override; `reduce_work` for gate G-5; `do_not_retry` for gate G-0, where the transport can never deliver a notification.

guidance.description: Prose instruction. For not-found, points at resources/list. Must not reveal whether an out-of-scope upstream exists.

retry_after_ms.description: Optional backoff hint; only meaningful with retry_later.

side_effects.description: A rejected subscribe or unsubscribe never mutates subscription state.

cause.description: Sanitized underlying error text, via labby_runtime::agent_error::sanitize_error_text. Absent for the caller-error gates.

$comment: Contract C-4: gate G-3 (unknown URI) and gate G-4 (out-of-scope upstream) must produce byte-identical data apart from `resource`. Do not add a field that distinguishes them — notably not the `denied_service` key used by resource_errors::route_scope, which is correct for reads but would leak upstream existence here.
